findings.evidence: IntegralRpow.lean:48-52 states only the cubic; Mathlib offers nothing above `integral_rpow` (upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Integrals/Basic.lean:147), so this file is the project's only statement of the fact and it stops at an arbitrary degree.
findings.fix: State the arbitrary-degree form, e.g. `theorem integral_poly_mul_rpow (a : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) {s : ℝ} (hs : -1 < s) : ∫ z in (0:ℝ)..1, (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a k * z ^ k) * z ^ s = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a k / (s + k + 1)` (induction on `n`, same `Real.rpow_add_one`/`integral_rpow` ingredients), and keep `integral_cubic_mul_rpow` as a one-line corollary via `Finset.sum_range_succ`. Callers and the public name survive unchanged, so this does not conflict with the api-design thread that made the lemma public.
findings.issue: `integral_cubic_mul_rpow` hard-codes degree 3 (`a₀ a₁ a₂ a₃`) in a general-purpose `Mathematics/Calculus` module. Degree 3 is not a boundary of the mathematics, only of today's call sites — the module docstring says so ("The regular parts of the splitting kernels of collinear evolution are cubic polynomials"), and three of the four callers pass dead zero coefficients: `0 / (n + 3) + 0 / (n + 4)` (LeadingOrder.lean:272), `0 / (N - 2 + 4)` (:289), `0 / (N - 1 + 4)` (:313). Only `moment_pgg` (:343) uses all four.

findings.evidence: NormalForm.lean has no such lemma (its results are `pair_pow`, `moment_natCast_add_one`, the congr-ae trio, `mellinDis_regular_eq_moment`, `pair_smul`/`moment_smul`). All ingredients already exist: `plusFunctional_add_left` (PlusFunctional.lean:219), `plusFunctional_const_mul_left` (:196), `plusFunctional_of_intervalIntegrable` (:241). Checked numerically for pqq: `p/(1-z) + r = 2C_F/(1-z) - C_F(1+z) = C_F(1+z²)/(1-z)` and `d + ∫₀¹ r = 3/2 C_F - 3/2 C_F = 0`, i.e. `pair_pqq` is exactly the instance.
findings.fix: Add the general lemma to `Kernel/NormalForm.lean` with hypotheses `hφ₁`, `IntervalIntegrable (fun z => P.regular z * φ z) volume 0 1` and `IntervalIntegrable P.regular volume 0 1`, then obtain `pair_pqq` by instantiating at `pqq c` and rewriting `2 C_F (1-z)⁻¹ - C_F (1+z) = C_F (1+z²)/(1-z)` with `plusFunctional_congr_ae_left`; the `pair_pgg` step after `plusOneMinus_id_mul` can use it too.
findings.issue: `pair_pqq` proves inline a fact that holds for every `KernelForm`: `P.pair φ = plusFunctional (fun z => P.plusCoeff * (1 - z)⁻¹ + P.regular z) φ + φ 1 * (P.deltaCoeff + ∫₀¹ P.regular)`. The whole body (lines 209-242: rewrite `(1+z²)/(1-z)` as `2(1-z)⁻¹ + -(1+z)`, `plusFunctional_add_left`, `plusFunctional_const_mul_left`, `plusFunctional_of_intervalIntegrable`, and the computation `∫₀¹ (1+z) = 3/2` cancelling `deltaCoeff = 3/2 C_F`) is that general argument specialised to one kernel. The delta coefficient cancelling against `-∫₀¹ r` is the general mechanism, recorded here only for `pqq`.

summary: Hypotheses are sharp and the N=1,2 results are correctly derived from the general moments. Two wrong-level items: the new calculus lemma is truncated at degree 3 for no mathematical reason, and the normal-form-to-plus-form conversion is proved only for pqq instead of for KernelForm.
